questions.stem: Which receptor family produces a response within milliseconds because the receptor and the effector are the same protein?
questions.explanation: Ligand-gated ion channels (e.g., nicotinic ACh receptor) open directly on agonist binding, within milliseconds. B: GPCRs work over seconds via G-proteins and second messengers. C: Kinase-linked receptors take hours (gene transcription). D: Cytokine receptors also act over hours. E: Nuclear receptors need transcription and protein synthesis (hours).

questions.stem: Through which G-protein and second-messenger pathway do α1-adrenoceptors and M3 muscarinic receptors act?

options.C: Direct opening of K⁺ channels by the G-protein
options.D: Gq → phospholipase C → IP3 and DAG

questions.explanation: α1 and M3 couple to Gq, activating phospholipase C (IP3/DAG → Ca²⁺). A: Gs/cAMP is used by β-adrenoceptors. B: Gi is used by α2. C: G-protein opening of K⁺ channels is the M2 mechanism in the heart. E: Guanylyl cyclase is linked to ANF receptors and isn't GPCR signaling here.

questions.stem: An asthmatic patient uses a salbutamol inhaler every hour for a day and notices each puff works less well. Which mechanism is mainly responsible for this rapid loss of response?

options.A: Down-regulation by reduced receptor gene expression over weeks
options.B: Receptor phosphorylation by βARK and binding of β-arrestin

questions.explanation: Rapid (seconds–minutes), reversible desensitization: GRK (βARK) phosphorylates the agonist-occupied receptor, then β-arrestin uncouples it from Gs. A: Down-regulation is slower (hours–days). C: Enzyme induction is a PK process that takes days. D: Antibodies aren't the mechanism. E: Glucocorticoids aren't involved, and they tend to restore β-receptor responsiveness.

questions.stem: In a population study, a drug has an ED50 of 10 mg for its therapeutic effect and a TD50 of 400 mg for a toxic effect. What is its therapeutic index?
questions.explanation: TI = TD50 / ED50 = 400 / 10 = 40. A: Inverts the ratio. B: Divides by 100. C: Subtracts instead of dividing. D: Multiplies instead of dividing.

questions.stem: Researchers count how many of 100 patients obtain headache relief at each dose of an analgesic. Which type of curve and parameter are they generating?
questions.explanation: An all-or-none effect counted across a population gives a quantal curve; ED50 is the dose at which 50% respond. A: Graded curves measure response size in one individual (EC50). B: Emax belongs to graded curves. D: KD comes from binding studies. E: Bmax is the binding capacity, not a quantal parameter.

questions.stem: A patient's pain is unchanged when ibuprofen is increased above its usual maximal dose, but he develops dyspepsia. Which concept explains this?
questions.explanation: Above the ceiling dose, further increases give no extra analgesia but add side effects. A: The threshold dose is the lowest dose with a detectable effect. B: Tachyphylaxis is a rapidly fading response to repeated doses. C: Spare receptors increase sensitivity. D: Inverse agonism reduces constitutive receptor activity.

questions.stem: A traveler develops profuse watery diarrhea after drinking contaminated water. Stool contains a toxin that ADP-ribosylates a G-protein α subunit. What is the direct intracellular consequence in enterocytes?

options.A: Inhibition of Gi, preventing cAMP from falling
options.B: Gs locked in the GTP-bound state → persistently ↑ cAMP
options.C: Activation of Gq → ↑ IP3 and Ca²⁺

questions.explanation: Cholera toxin prevents Gsα from hydrolyzing GTP, so adenylyl cyclase stays on → high cAMP → CFTR opening and Cl⁻/water secretion. A: Gi inhibition is pertussis toxin's action. C: Gq isn't the target. D: Heat-stable E. coli toxin raises cGMP; it doesn't lower it. E: CFTR is opened, not blocked.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old nonsmoking woman has lung adenocarcinoma with an activating mutation in a receptor tyrosine kinase that normally binds epidermal growth factor. Which drug directly targets this receptor's kinase activity?
questions.explanation: Erlotinib is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. A: Trastuzumab is an antibody against HER2. B: Tofacitinib inhibits JAK (cytokine receptor signaling). D: Imatinib inhibits BCR-ABL. E: Rituximab targets CD20 on B cells.

questions.stem: For the same quantal effect, drug A has an ED50 of 2 mg and drug B an ED50 of 50 mg. Which conclusion is justified?

options.A: A produces a larger maximal effect than B
options.B: A has a wider therapeutic index than B
options.C: B is 25 times more potent than A
options.D: A is 25 times more potent than B
options.E: A is 25 times more selective than B

questions.explanation: Potency compares the doses needed for the same effect: 50 ÷ 2 = 25. A more potent drug isn't necessarily more effective or safer. A: Potency says nothing about maximal effect. B: The therapeutic index also needs the TD50. C: Reverses it; a lower ED50 means higher potency. E: Selectivity compares one drug's ED50 values for two different effects.

questions.stem: A patient with an acute asthma attack receives a systemic glucocorticoid plus an inhaled β2-agonist. Why can't the glucocorticoid be relied on alone for immediate relief?

options.A: Its receptor alters gene transcription, so effects lag 30 min to hours
options.B: Its G-protein-coupled receptor desensitizes within minutes
options.C: It opens a ligand-gated channel that closes within milliseconds
options.D: It is only a partial agonist at β2-adrenoceptors
options.E: Its kinase-linked receptor is rapidly down-regulated

questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids are lipid-soluble and act on intracellular (nuclear) receptors; new proteins must be made, so effects take 30 min to hours and then outlast plasma levels. B: Glucocorticoid receptors aren't GPCRs; desensitization over minutes is a GPCR feature (e.g., β2). C: Ligand-gated channels act in milliseconds and would give rapid relief. D: Glucocorticoids don't act at β2-adrenoceptors. E: They don't act through kinase-linked receptors.
